summary.name: Harbofly
summary.one_liner: Harbofly is a free, open-source, notarized native macOS menu bar app that finds developer build artifacts and caches (DerivedData, node_modules, Docker images, package caches) and frees disk space by moving them to the Trash first.
use_cases: Free up space taken by Xcode DerivedData and simulator caches
Find and remove old node_modules folders from stalled projects
Clear npm, Yarn, Homebrew and SwiftPM caches safely
Review Docker images and AI model caches before deleting them
Automate cleanup of safe caches at login, logout, or low disk
summary.what_it_does: Harbofly scans folders such as ~/Development and ~/Library for build artifacts, caches and AI model files, and shows each item's path, size and a safety tier (green: regenerates automatically; yellow: recreated but costly; read-only items it never touches). Nothing dangerous is pre-selected, and deletions go to the Trash by default so they can be restored. It flags projects inactive for 90+ days and warns when a project has uncommitted or unpushed git work, reading this from the local repo offline. It also offers opt-in auto-clean of only green caches, an app uninstaller that moves leftovers to the Trash, and a login-item manager that disables agents by moving them aside. A command-line binary provides harbofly scan and harbofly clean --dry-run.
notable: Moves deletions to the Trash by default, so they can be restored
Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple; open source end to end and auditable
Native Swift with no Electron; analytics are opt-in and off by default
Git-aware stale project detection that works offline
caveats: Analytics and update checks are optional and can be turned off; scan and cleanup work offline
Yellow-tier items such as Docker images are never pre-selected and carry recreation cost
Only macOS is named on the page
